newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam CEO says share buybacks possible.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam CEO says share buybacks possible.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp chief executive Albert Dunlap said on Tuesday his company overhaul will quickly eliminate debt and allow the appliance maker to consider share buybacks in the near future.
"Share repurchases are one option," Dunlap said in a telephone conference call with investors. "We could merge. We could acquire."
Dunlap said he and his managers would during the next two months concentrate on implementing the sweeping company restructuring announced earlier.
Sunbeam plans to shut or sell dozens of facilities, halve its workforce to 6,000, sell some businesses, and take a fourth-quarter, pre-tax charge of $300 million.
Dunlap also promised to double Sunbeam's sales to $2 billion by 1999, mainly by selling through new channels, going overseas and bringing new products to market.

Dunlap said he expects Sunbeam, a maker of small appliances and barbecues, to be net debt free in the coming year and to generate lots of cash in the next three years from asset sales and by spending less on plants and working capital.
